incident-bot: PagerDuty ALERT fired -> PD-CRIT proxy-5xx-rate-usw (threshold 0.5%) assigned to @alex. Link: https://pagerduty.example/alerts/PD123456 :rotating_light:

alex: ACK — i'm on it. grabbing dashboards and logs :eyes:

sam: saw a short spike on ngi-proxy 5xxs ~10:12am, might be canary traffic. no maps of customer errors yet.

alex: running quick query: `sum(rate(proxy_5xx_total[1m])) by (pod)` -> spikes from `proxy-canary-1` and `proxy-canary-2` only.

alex: running `kubectl get pods -n infra -l app=proxy-canary -o wide` and tailing logs
```
kubectl logs proxy-canary-1 -n infra --tail=80
2026-03-15T10:11:58Z ERROR upstream_timeout id=abc123 upstream=backend-a timeout=30ms
2026-03-15T10:12:00Z WARN circuit_breaker tripped for route /v1/health
2026-03-15T10:12:01Z ERROR upstream_reset connection reset by peer
```

marta: @alex i just noticed the canary job ramp is at 200rps — that seems higher than expected. i'm pausing it now.

marta: `kubectl scale job proxy-canary --replicas=0 -n infra` -> paused.

sam: dashboards showing 5xxs dropping back down within 20s of pause. latency and error budget graphs normalizing. :white_check_mark:

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: PD-CRIT PD123456 auto-resolved at 7365432132 (duration 32s) — no escalation.

alex: confirm no customer-facing errors in Sentry or external monitoring. quick grep of recent 5xx by customer_id shows zeros.

alex: adding a sticky note — this was noisy synthetic canary ramp that exceeded backend capacity; no customer impact. will file a follow-up with infra-canary team to cap ramp and add guardrails.

marta: filing follow-up ticket: `INFRA-7893` with suggested fix: add rate limiter in canary runner + early abort on >0.2% 5xx.

dinesh: thanks all — i'm next oncall at 10:30, i'll monitor handoff. ping me if it reappears.

alex: closing thread. PD auto-resolved, non-impacting, action items created. :thumbsup:

[reactions summary: incident-bot message reacted :exclamation:, alex message reacted :eyes:, sam reacted :white_check_mark: ]
